subject: Quick pre-demo check: concurrency, timeline & SSO for AtlasPay
messages:
From: Samira Khan <samira@atlaspay.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 08:12:00 +0000
Subject: Requesting a short demo — signed up today

Hi Evelyn,

I signed AtlasPay up for the self-serve tier this morning and wanted to follow up to get a short walkthrough of Redwood — primarily around latency (we're sensitive), SSO, and what a pilot would look like.

High level:
- Use case: reconciliation & fraud-assist in payment flows (server-side calls from our reconciliation pipeline).
- Current footprint: ~5k API calls/day across environments; expecting growth to ~150k/mo in Q4.
- Peak: we see bursts during settlement windows (~150 concurrent calls for short spikes).

We'd love a 20–30 minute demo next week to cover deployment modes and whether dedicated capacity makes sense for us. Our CTO (Raj Patel) will join if possible — he prefers ETEA-friendly times (US morning or UK afternoon).

Also: is there a short pre-demo checklist we should fill so the call is focused?

Thanks,
Samira
Samira Khan
Head of Integrations, AtlasPay
samira@atlaspay.com

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Khan <samira@atlaspay.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 12:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Requesting a short demo — signed up today

Hi Samira — welcome and congrats on signing up. Happy to run a focused 25-minute session that covers: quick product fit, latency/throughput options, SSO checklist, and a recommended pilot ramp.

Quick pre-demo questions so we can tailor the session:
1) Peak concurrency during settlement windows — you mentioned ~150 concurrent calls. Is that sustained for more than a few minutes or is it a sub-minute spike?
2) Typical request size (average tokens / payload size) and whether calls are streaming or single-response.
3) Timeline: when would you like pilot traffic to begin (date range)?
4) Data residency / compliance needs: do you require EU-only hosting or specific retention controls?
5) Who will be the technical point of contact on your side (CC Raj if you want him looped in formally)?

I pasted three proposed 25-minute slots here: https://cal.com/evelyn/30 — feel free to pick one and we'll lock it.

I've attached a short pre-demo checklist that covers SSO requirements and what we'll ask during the call. If you can drop an estimated monthly token count (or CSV) that helps our perf team prepare.

—Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
evelyn_hart@redwood.ai

From: Samira Khan <samira@atlaspay.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: Raj Patel <raj.patel@atlaspay.com>
Date: Wed, 16 Sep 2026 09:40:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Requesting a short demo — signed up today

Hi Evelyn — thanks for the quick reply and the checklist. Answers below: 

1) Peak concurrency: the settlement windows are short bursts (1–3 minutes) with ~150 concurrent calls; the rest of the day concurrency is <20.
2) Request sizes: average payload ~600 tokens (mostly structured JSON with 3–4 fields of text); responses are single-response generation (no streaming).
3) Timeline: wed like to kick off a small pilot by the week of Oct 4 (production-ready in November ideally).
4) Residency: primary operations in US; no EU-only requirement today but would like region-aware routing as we expand.
5) POC contact: Raj (cc'd) + myself. Raj handles infra and capacity decisions.

We prefer US morning slots. I selected a slot on your calendar for Sep 17 at 10:30am PT but if that doesn't work for the CTO's calendar we can reschedule.

Attached a quick CSV with monthly estimates.

Thanks,
Samira

Thanks for the details — this is very helpful and gives us a clear pilot recommendation.

Summary / what we'll cover on the call (25m):
- Short product orientation (3m): hosted vs dedicated tradeoffs for bursts.
- Latency & concurrency patterns (7m): how prefix/KV caching and autoscaling help during 1–3 minute settlement spikes.
- Pilot setup (8m): suggested pilot capacity (start with a single dedicated slot + hosted fallback), ramp schedule to production, and minimal SSO checklist items.
- Next steps & wrap (7m): calendar for pilot kickoff and handoffs.

I've added Monica (our SDR) to help with calendar logistics and Ben (our Solutions Architect) to join the call for the ramp discussion. Monica will send a calendar invite that includes a short agenda and the pre-demo checklist.

If Raj can't make the Sep 17 10:30am PT time, please reply with two alternative US-morning windows and Monica will coordinate. Otherwise, see you Sep 17.

Best,
Evelyn
